# Overview

In this vignette, we will use the Seurat object processed in the previous step of the course to infer and visualize cell-cell communication in spatial transcriptomics data. The workflow combines two complementary approaches:

1.  **CellChat** estimates ligand--receptor interactions between spot clusters [@Jin2021CellChat; @Jin2025CellChat]; and
2.  **RGraphSpace/PathwaySpace** represents these interactions between neighboring spots and projects the signal onto the tissue [@RGraphSpace2026; @Tercan2025PathwaySpace; @Ellrott2025CancerSubtypes].

The input object must be `data/brain.RDS`, generated by the quality control, preprocessing and clustering vignette. Although it contains both the anterior and posterior sections of the `stxBrain` dataset, we will keep only the `anterior` region right after loading it. Thus, all calculations, results and plots in this vignette will be produced using that region only. The object also contains the expression normalized by `SCTransform()` and the Seurat clusters [@Hao2023Seurat].

At the end, the table of projected spot-to-spot communications will be saved as:

``` text
resultados/spot-spot_commu_anterior.rds
```

> **How to interpret the result:** CellChat estimates communication at the group level, which in this analysis are the Seurat clusters. The spot--spot table is a projection of these estimates onto pairs of spatially close spots that match the source and target clusters. Therefore, it does not represent an independent CellChat inference for each individual pair of spots.

# Set up the environment

## Folder structure

Before running the code, set the working directory to the `vinhetas/` folder. In RStudio, use **Session \> Set Working Directory \> To Source File Location**.

``` text
Curso_ST/
|-- data/
|   `-- brain.RDS
|-- imagens/
|-- resultados/
`-- vinhetas/
    |-- CellChat_Comunicacao_Celular_PathwaySpace.Rmd
    `-- CellChat_Comunicacao_Celular_PathwaySpace.html
```

```{r define-directories}
vignettes_dir <- getwd()
course_dir <- dirname(vignettes_dir)
data_dir <- file.path(course_dir, "data")
images_dir <- file.path(course_dir, "imagens")
results_dir <- file.path(course_dir, "resultados")

dir.create(images_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Check the required packages

Installation of all packages and their dependencies is centralized in `Configuracao_do_ambiente_RStudio.Rmd`. Run that first vignette, restart the R session, and then use the chunk below only to confirm that the environment is ready.

```{r check-packages}
cellchat_packages <- c(
  "CellChat", "RGraphSpace", "PathwaySpace", "Seurat", "SeuratObject",
  "dplyr", "tibble", "tidyr", "ggplot2", "RANN", "future"
)

missing_packages <- cellchat_packages[
  !vapply(cellchat_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Run Configuracao_do_ambiente_RStudio.Rmd first. ",
    "Missing packages: ",
    paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", ")
  )
}
```

## Load the packages

We load the packages used for inference, data manipulation and visualization. This vignette uses Seurat 5.5.1 as its reference version.

```{r load-packages, message=FALSE}
library("CellChat")
library("RGraphSpace")
library("PathwaySpace")
library("Seurat")
library("SeuratObject")
library("dplyr")
library("tibble")
library("tidyr")
library("ggplot2")

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

packageVersion("Seurat")
```

# Load the previously produced spatial object

After loading the full object, `subset()` discards all spots from the posterior region. The corresponding spatial image is also removed from the object, keeping only the `anterior1` section for the following steps.

```{r load-brain}
brain <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "brain.RDS"))
brain <- subset(brain, subset = region == "anterior")

DefaultAssay(brain) <- "SCT"
Idents(brain) <- "seurat_clusters"

if (length(Images(brain)) != 1L) {
  stop("The anterior region subset must keep exactly one spatial image.")
}

image_name <- Images(brain)[1]

brain
table(brain$region)
```

The expected result is an object with 2,696 spots and a single image named `anterior1`.

# Prepare the CellChat inputs

CellChat requires four main components for spatial data:

-   `data.input`: normalized gene-by-spot matrix;
-   `meta`: cluster and sample labels;
-   `spatial.locs`: full-resolution spatial coordinates; and
-   `spatial.factors`: factors used to convert pixels to micrometers.

## Normalized expression and metadata

The normalized layer of the `SCT` assay provides the expression used by CellChat. The metadata associate each spot with its Seurat cluster and with the single spatial sample kept.

```{r prepare-expression-metadata}
data.input <- LayerData(brain, assay = "SCT", layer = "data")
anterior_spots <- Cells(brain[[image_name]])
data.input <- data.input[, anterior_spots, drop = FALSE]

brain_metadata <- brain[[]]

meta <- data.frame(
  labels = paste0("cluster_",
    brain_metadata[colnames(data.input), "seurat_clusters"]),
  samples = image_name,
  row.names = colnames(data.input)
)

meta$labels <- factor(meta$labels)
meta$samples <- factor(meta$samples, levels = image_name)

table(meta$labels, meta$samples)
```

## Spatial coordinates and factors

In Seurat 5.5.1, `GetTissueCoordinates()` returns the unscaled `VisiumV2` positions in the `x` and `y` columns. After aligning the spots to the columns of the expression matrix, we estimate the factor that converts pixels to micrometers. For Visium, we assume 100 µm between the centers of adjacent spots and 55 µm as the theoretical spot diameter.

```{r prepare-coordinates}
spatial.locs <- GetTissueCoordinates(
  brain, image = image_name, scale = NULL)
spatial.locs <- as.data.frame(spatial.locs[, c("x", "y"), drop = FALSE])
spatial.locs <- spatial.locs[colnames(data.input), , drop = FALSE]

spot.size <- 55
center_distance <- 100
distances <- computeCellDistance(coordinates = spatial.locs)
min_distance <- min(distances[distances > 0])

spatial.factors <- data.frame(
  ratio = center_distance / min_distance,
  tol = spot.size / 2,
  row.names = image_name
)

spatial.factors
head(spatial.locs)
```

## Create the CellChat object

With expression, labels, coordinates and scale in the same order, we build the spatial object that will be used for inference.

```{r create-cellchat}
cellchat <- createCellChat(
  object = data.input, meta = meta, group.by = "labels",
  datatype = "spatial", coordinates = spatial.locs,
  spatial.factors = spatial.factors
)

cellchat
```

# Define the ligand--receptor interaction database

Since the `stxBrain` dataset is from mouse, we will use `CellChatDB.mouse`. To keep the run time suitable for a teaching activity, the analysis will be restricted to the **Secreted Signaling** category.

```{r define-cellchatdb, fig.width=7, fig.height=3}
CellChatDB <- CellChatDB.mouse
showDatabaseCategory(CellChatDB)

CellChatDB.use <- subsetDB(CellChatDB,
  search = "Secreted Signaling", key = "annotation")

cellchat@DB <- CellChatDB.use
```

# Preprocess the expression data

CellChat keeps the genes present in the selected database and identifies overexpressed genes and interactions. The `plan()` function with the `multisession` option allows this step to be distributed across up to four R processes (*cores*).

```{r preprocess-cellchat}
cellchat <- subsetData(cellchat)

future::plan("multisession", workers = 4)

cellchat <- identifyOverExpressedGenes(cellchat)
cellchat <- identifyOverExpressedInteractions(cellchat, variable.both = FALSE)
```

# Infer communication between clusters

In this step, interactions and contact-dependent communication are restricted to 100 µm, approximately the distance between the centers of adjacent Visium spots. This cutoff helps speed up the analysis.

For the classroom demonstration, `nboot` was limited to 10 to compute faster. `nboot` is the number of permutation tests used to calculate the p-values.

**Caution:** this is the most computationally expensive step of the vignette; it may take several minutes to run.

```{r infer-communication}
cellchat <- computeCommunProb(
  cellchat, type = "triMean", distance.use = TRUE,
  interaction.range = 100, scale.distance = 0.01,
  contact.range = 100, contact.dependent = TRUE,
  contact.knn.k = 6, nboot = 10
)

cellchat <- filterCommunication(cellchat, min.cells = 10)
```

We extract only the interactions with a *p*-value below 0.05. Converting the groups to character will make the joins with the spot tables easier.

```{r extract-communications}
df.net <- subsetCommunication(cellchat, thresh = 0.05)

df.net <- df.net %>%
  mutate(source = as.character(source), target = as.character(target))

head(df.net)
```

# Project communications onto spot pairs

Now we will identify the pairs of spots in the anterior region that are separated by up to 100 µm. Then, each pair will be assigned its source and target clusters and combined with the interactions inferred by CellChat.

```{r identify-neighboring-spots}
interaction.range <- 100

coords_um <- spatial.locs * spatial.factors[image_name, "ratio"]
distance_matrix <- as.matrix(dist(coords_um))
diag(distance_matrix) <- Inf

indices <- which(distance_matrix <= interaction.range, arr.ind = TRUE)

spot.pairs <- tibble(
  source_spot = rownames(distance_matrix)[indices[, 1]],
  target_spot = colnames(distance_matrix)[indices[, 2]],
  distance_um = distance_matrix[indices],
  sample = image_name
)

spot.groups <- tibble(spot = rownames(cellchat@meta),
  group = as.character(cellchat@idents))

spot.pairs <- spot.pairs %>%
  left_join(spot.groups, by = c("source_spot" = "spot")) %>%
  rename(source = group) %>%
  left_join(spot.groups, by = c("target_spot" = "spot")) %>%
  rename(target = group)

head(spot.pairs)
```

The interactions inferred for each cluster pair are then associated with the matching spot pairs. The resulting table is sorted and saved for reuse.

```{r combine-and-save-communications}
spot.to.spot.communication <- spot.pairs %>%
  inner_join(df.net, by = c("source", "target")) %>%
  arrange(sample, source_spot, target_spot,
    pathway_name, interaction_name)

head(spot.to.spot.communication)

saveRDS(
  spot.to.spot.communication,
  file = file.path(results_dir,
    "spot-spot_commu_anterior.rds")
)
```

# Build the spatial network in RGraphSpace

The `GraphSpace` object brings together the coordinates, metadata, normalized expression and image of the anterior section. The low-resolution coordinates allow the network to be correctly overlaid on the tissue image.

```{r build-graphspace-anterior}
plot_spots <- anterior_spots

gs_coords <- GetTissueCoordinates(
  brain, image = image_name, scale = "lowres"
)
gs_coords <- gs_coords[
  plot_spots, c("x", "y"), drop = FALSE
]

gs_metadata <- brain[[]][plot_spots, , drop = FALSE]
gs <- GraphSpace(cbind(gs_coords, gs_metadata))

gs_fdata(gs) <- LayerData(
  brain, assay = "SCT", layer = "data"
)[, plot_spots, drop = FALSE]

gs_image(gs) <- GetImage(
  brain[[image_name]], mode = "raster"
)

gs <- normalizeGraphSpace(gs)
```

First, we check the position of the clusters on the image before adding the proximity relationships.

```{r plot-clusters-graphspace}
spatial_theme <- theme_gspace_coords(
  theme = "th3", is_norm = TRUE,
  xlab = "Spatial coordinate 1", ylab = "Spatial coordinate 2"
)

cpal1 <- DiscretePalette(nlevels(gs$seurat_clusters), "polychrome")

ggplot(gs) +
  annotation_gspace_image(gs) +
  geom_nodespace(mapping = aes(colour = seurat_clusters),
    size = 1, pch = 19) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cpal1) +
  theme_gspace_legend(discrete_colour = TRUE) +
  spatial_theme
```

## Add the proximity relationships

The function below connects each spot to its six nearest neighbors, following the hexagonal layout expected for a Visium slide. Spots at the edges may have fewer neighbors.

```{r define-proximity-network}
proximityNetwork <- function(gs, nnei = 6) {
  nodes <- gs@nodes

  neighbors <- RANN::nn2(nodes[, c("x", "y")],
    nodes[, c("x", "y")], k = nnei + 1)

  dists <- as.data.frame(neighbors$nn.dists[, 2:(nnei + 1)])
  indices <- as.data.frame(neighbors$nn.idx[, 2:(nnei + 1)])

  typical_distance <- 1 / mean(1 / dists$V1)
  keep <- dists
  keep[, 1] <- TRUE
  keep[, 2:ncol(keep)] <-
    dists[, 2:ncol(dists)] >= 0.95 * typical_distance &
    dists[, 2:ncol(dists)] <= 1.05 * typical_distance

  edge_matrix <- keep * indices
  edge_matrix$from <- row.names(edge_matrix)

  edges <- edge_matrix %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -from, names_to = "neighbor", values_to = "to") %>%
    filter(to != 0) %>%
    transmute(from = as.numeric(from), to = as.numeric(to),
      v1 = pmin(from, to), v2 = pmax(from, to)) %>%
    distinct(v1, v2) %>%
    transmute(from = nodes$name[v1], to = nodes$name[v2])

  gs_add_edges(gs) <- edges
  gs
}
```

Before creating the edges, we zoom into a central area to look at the spots alone. This view will serve as a comparison for the network built in the next chunk.

```{r plot-network-without-edges}
ggplot(gs) +
  annotation_gspace_image(gs) +
  geom_edgespace() +
  geom_nodespace(mapping = aes(colour = seurat_clusters),
    size = 3, pch = 19) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cpal1) +
  theme_gspace_legend(discrete_colour = TRUE) +
  spatial_theme +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.4, 0.6), ylim = c(0.4, 0.6))
```

Now we apply `proximityNetwork()` and repeat the zoomed view. The lines show which spots will be considered neighbors when projecting the communications.

```{r add-and-plot-edges}
gs <- proximityNetwork(gs)

ggplot(gs) +
  annotation_gspace_image(gs) +
  geom_edgespace() +
  geom_nodespace(mapping = aes(colour = seurat_clusters),
    size = 3, pch = 19) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cpal1) +
  theme_gspace_legend(discrete_colour = TRUE) +
  spatial_theme +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.4, 0.6), ylim = c(0.4, 0.6))
```

# Associate communications with the proximity edges

The `GraphSpace` edges are undirected, but ligand--receptor communication has a source and a target. Therefore, we will create both orientations of each edge before associating them with the CellChat communications.

```{r associate-edges-communications}
edges <- gs@edges %>% select(name1, name2)

directed_edges <- bind_rows(
  edges,
  edges %>% transmute(name1 = name2, name2 = name1)
) %>%
  distinct()

spotCom_dt <- directed_edges %>%
  inner_join(
    spot.to.spot.communication %>% filter(sample == image_name),
    by = c("name1" = "source_spot", "name2" = "target_spot")
  )

spotCom_dt$arrowType <- 1

available_interactions <- spotCom_dt %>%
  select(ligand, receptor, interaction_name) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ligand), !is.na(receptor)) %>%
  distinct()

head(available_interactions)
```

# Project an interaction with PathwaySpace

The `communication_pathwayspace()` function keeps the spots involved in an interaction, builds the `PathwaySpace` object, sums the ligand and receptor expression, and projects this signal onto the network. Names separated by underscores are treated as complexes made up of more than one gene.

```{r define-pathwayspace-function}
communication_pathwayspace <- function(gs, lig, recep, spotCom_dt) {
  communications <- spotCom_dt %>% filter(ligand == lig, receptor == recep)

  selected_spots <- unique(c(communications$name1, communications$name2))

  gs_selected <- gs_subset_nodes(gs, selected_spots)
  pspace_obj <- buildPathwaySpace(gs_selected)

  spot_distances <- getNearestNode(pspace_obj)
  pdist <- mean(spot_distances$dist)

  pspace_obj <- silhouetteMapping(pspace_obj, baseline = 0.1)

  resolve_features <- function(label, available_features) {
    if (label %in% available_features) {
      return(label)
    }

    components <- strsplit(label, "_", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    available_features[match(tolower(components),
      tolower(available_features))]
  }

  available_features <- colnames(pspace_obj@fdata)
  ligand_features <- resolve_features(lig, available_features)
  receptor_features <- resolve_features(recep, available_features)

  if (anyNA(c(ligand_features, receptor_features))) {
    stop("The ligand or receptor was not found in the expression data.")
  }

  ligand_signal <- rowSums(as.matrix(
    pspace_obj@fdata[, ligand_features, drop = FALSE]))
  receptor_signal <- rowSums(as.matrix(
    pspace_obj@fdata[, receptor_features, drop = FALSE]))

  vertexSignal(pspace_obj) <- ligand_signal + receptor_signal

  pspace_obj <- circularProjection(
    pspace_obj, decay.fun = weibullDecay(decay = 0.5, pdist = pdist),
    aggregate.fun = signalAggregation("wmean"),
    k = gs_vcount(pspace_obj))

  pspace_obj
}
```

## Visualize an example

We will use the first interaction available in the anterior region. If you prefer to investigate a specific pair, replace `example_ligand` and `example_receptor` with the desired symbols.

```{r plot-example-interaction}
if (nrow(available_interactions) == 0) {
  stop("No interaction was associated with the edges of the anterior region.")
}

example_ligand <- available_interactions$ligand[1]
example_receptor <- available_interactions$receptor[1]

pspace_obj <- communication_pathwayspace(
  gs = gs, lig = example_ligand, recep = example_receptor,
  spotCom_dt = spotCom_dt)

example_plot <- ggplot(pspace_obj) +
  annotation_gspace_image(pspace_obj) +
  annotation_pspace_signal(pspace_obj, si.alpha = 0.25) +
  spatial_theme + labs(
    title = paste(example_ligand, "-", example_receptor))

example_plot
```

# Save the interaction figures

For the classroom activity, the first three interactions will be exported. To generate all figures, replace the definition of `n_interactions` with `nrow(available_interactions)`.

```{r save-interaction-figures}
n_interactions <- min(3, nrow(available_interactions))

for (i in seq_len(n_interactions)) {
  ligand <- available_interactions$ligand[i]
  receptor <- available_interactions$receptor[i]

  pspace_i <- communication_pathwayspace(
    gs = gs, lig = ligand, recep = receptor, spotCom_dt = spotCom_dt)

  plot_i <- ggplot(pspace_i) +
    annotation_gspace_image(pspace_i) +
    annotation_pspace_signal(pspace_i, si.alpha = 0.25) +
    spatial_theme + labs(title = paste(ligand, "-", receptor))

  file_name <- paste0("CellChat_PathwaySpace_", image_name,
    "_", ligand, "-", receptor, ".png")

  file_name <- gsub("[^[:alnum:]_.-]", "_", file_name)

  ggsave(filename = file.path(images_dir, file_name),
    plot = plot_i, width = 9, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = 120, bg = "white")

  rm(pspace_i, plot_i)
  gc()
}
```

# Output files

When you finish the vignette, the following will be available:

-   `resultados/spot-spot_commu_anterior.rds`: table of projected communications between spots in the anterior region;
-   `imagens/CellChat_PathwaySpace_anterior1_<ligand>-<receptor>.png`: projections of the selected interactions; and
-   the intermediate objects `cellchat`, `gs`, `spot.to.spot.communication` and `spotCom_dt` in the R session.
